Trump just commented on inflation and the Fed—says inflation is "too high" but wants Chair Warsh to stay independent. Also noted he "still has confidence" in Warsh even after today's rate hike.

Interesting dynamic here. Presidents usually avoid commenting on Fed decisions to preserve that independence firewall. But Trump's never been shy about his views on rates.

Market's watching this closely. Any hint of political pressure on the Fed tends to spook bond traders and create volatility in rate-sensitive sectors. The "confidence" language is reassuring, but the inflation comment signals he wants easier policy.

For now, the Fed's path seems intact. But if inflation stays sticky and Trump keeps talking, this could get messy. Rate expectations and dollar strength will be key to watch.

🚨 Massive Setback for Crypto — CLARITY Act Failed Again? But Backup Plan Available...

We now know the CLARITY Act failed to advance in the Senate after a 49-50 procedural vote. The bill needed 60 votes, so this is a major setback for crypto regulation in the US But this does not mean the bill is permanently dead. 
$BNB $ASTER $SYN 

So what happens next?

The backup plan is the SEC and CFTC. SEC Chair Paul Atkins said the agency's crypto agenda will continue with or without congressional legislation. The CFTC has also prepared possible rules for crypto markets using its existing authority. 

This could mean clearer rules for exchanges, token issuers, spot markets and derivatives without waiting for Congress. However, agency rules cannot fully replace a complete law and may face legal challenges or future changes.

The vote caused fresh pressure across crypto, but the market reaction is not only about regulation. Macro conditions and leverage are also important.

The CLARITY Act failure delays full regulatory clarity, but it does not stop the SEC and CFTC from moving forward. Now the key question is whether regulators can deliver practical rules while Congress remains divided.
